key_insight: Cancer is common among patients with cardiovascular disease and risk factors, with pooled active cancer prevalence reaching about 4%–6% in several groups and any-cancer prevalence highest in atrial fibrillation.
clinical_relevance: These findings support routine cardiovascular-oncology awareness and multidisciplinary care because cancer burden is substantial across CAD, HF, AF, stroke, PAD, valvular disease, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes.
method: Systematic review and meta-analysis of PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus (2010–July 2024).
Pooled prevalence estimated with one-step generalized linear mixed models.
Included 676 studies with roughly 180 million participants overall; 59 studies informed active-cancer analyses.
evidence_signal: The analysis pooled prevalence estimates across very large real-world cohorts, with active cancer prevalence reported in patients with type 2 DM, HF, stroke, CAD, VHD, and AF.
watch_item: Prevalence estimates are highly heterogeneous across diseases and study settings, so they should be interpreted as population-level summaries rather than patient-specific risk predictions.
paper_title: Prevalence of cancer in patients with cardiovascular diseases and risk factors: a systematic review and meta-analysis
